text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
-- The number of countries to join the NATO in the first stage of enlargement may increase to five from three, adding Romania and Slovenia to the Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary.
-- The government is discussing economic policy plans for the next three years. According to the forecast, economic growth may reach four percent next year.
-- Opposition MP's boycotted the meeting of the parliament's budget and social committees, saying that the time for preparing for the discussion of the pension reform draft laws had been too short.
-- Both the government and the opposition denies media news of their talks about the potential formation of a national front coalition.

-- The Government Supervision Office initiated police action against yet unknown persons because the state privatisation agency APV could not provide it with full data about contracts with privatisation advisors.
-- The Free Democrat's Alliance (SZDSZ), the junior member of the rulinh coalition, criticises a government accord with the Catholic church about returning confiscated church assets.
